title: Exogenous NO Delays Fruit Softening, Reduces Pathogen Incidence, and Modulates Phytohormone Levels During Sweet Cherry (Prunus avium L.) Postharvest Storage
content: The effect of exogenous nitric oxide (NO) treatment on the quality and health of sweet cherry (Prunus avium L.) cv. Bing fruits during postharvest storage was studied. After harvest, fruits were treated by immersion in: deionized water (control) or 0.1 mM GSNO (S-nitrosoglutathione), and stored under three conditions: 1) 7 d, 20 °C, 70% RH (SL); 2) 30 d, 0 °C, 95% RH (CS); and 3) 30 d, 0 °C, 95% RH followed by 7 d, 20 °C, 70% RH (CS+SL). Physicochemical quality parameters were evaluated, as well as natural incidence of diseases. GSNO treatment preserved fruit firmness without affecting other quality parameters and reduced the natural incidence of diseases, without showing a direct in vitro antifungal effect on common postharvest pathogens. Besides, GSNO treatment reduced ABA content in fruits after SL, as compared to control sweet cherries. Conversely, ABA increase was not prevented by GSNO under CS+SL and no effect was observed after CS. Likewise, GSNO treatment increased GA1 but reduced GA3 contents in fruits under SL, whereas both GAs decreased or remained unchanged under longer storage times. Salicylic acid levels decreased under CS and CS+SL in GSNO-treated cherries. GSNO modulation of growth-ripening related phytohormones and the induction of pathogen resistance seem to be targets of this signaling molecule, preserving the quality and health attributes required for cherries commercialization.
